title: Verb patterns: like doing, want to do
tagline: After like, want, go and let's — is it -ing or to? Here's how to choose.
exam: Speaking Part 1 — talking about your free time
why: Verb patterns like this decide whether the next word is -ing or to — one of the most common grammar points in Reading Part 5. They also make your Speaking Part 1 answers about hobbies sound natural: I enjoy playing…, I want to learn…

hook.text: Break time. Nadia says: "I love playing basketball!" Mateo shakes his head. "I hate playing it, but I want to try swimming." "Let's go swimming after school, then!" says Nadia.
hook.ask: Nadia and Mateo talk about sports in two different ways — with -ing and with to. Can you find one example of each?

diagrams.title: Build the sentence: -ing or to?
diagrams.caption: The first verb (like, want, go, let's) decides the shape of the second one.

diagrams.title: Adding -ing

rules.rule: One vowel + one consonant: double the consonant
Verb ending in -e: drop the e, + ing
Verb ending in -ie: change to -y, + ing

diagrams.caption: The spelling changes, but the job of -ing stays the same.

head: Pattern
Verbs
Example
rows: like, love, hate, enjoy, don't mind
want, need, would like, hope, decide, learn
It started raining. / It started to rain.

use.point: like, love, hate, enjoy, don't mind + -ing

examples.text: I don't mind waiting for the bus.
examples.note: don't mind + -ing = it's OK for me

use.point: want, need, would like, hope, decide, learn + to

examples.text: She needs to finish her project tonight.
I'd like to visit Cusco one day.
examples.note: would like + to, a polite way to say want

examples.text: Liam decided to join the football team.

examples.note: go shopping, go camping, go fishing…

examples.text: How about going to the cinema tonight?

use.point: start and begin — both patterns work

examples.note: start + to — the meaning is the same

watch_out.why: Enjoy is always followed by -ing, never to.
Want is always followed by to + base verb, not -ing.
Don't forget the -s with he/she/it in the present simple.

watch_out.wrong: I'd like going to the beach.
watch_out.right: I'd like to go to the beach.
watch_out.why: Would like is always followed by to, like a polite want.
Let's is followed by the base verb, with no to.
Don't mind is followed by -ing, not to.

l1.why: In Spanish the infinitive follows gustar; in English, like usually takes -ing.
Want is followed by to + base verb, not -ing.

l1.wrong: I go to swim on Saturdays.
l1.why: For sports and activities, English uses go + -ing, not go + to.
Don't mind takes -ing, like enjoy and like.
Hope is followed by to + base verb, not -ing.

remember.tip: Feelings (like, love, hate, enjoy) usually take -ing. Plans and wishes (want, need, hope) usually take to.

dialogue.title: Planning the weekend
dialogue.context: It's Friday afternoon. Liam, Nadia and Sofia plan what to do at the weekend.

lines.speaker: Liam
lines.text: I love playing football on Saturdays. Does anyone want to join?

lines.speaker: Nadia
lines.text: I don't mind watching, but I hate playing in the rain!

lines.speaker: Sofia
lines.text: How about going to the cinema instead, if it rains?

lines.speaker: Liam
lines.text: Good idea. I want to see the new film.

lines.speaker: Nadia
lines.text: I need to finish my project first, though.

lines.speaker: Liam
lines.text: I'd like to go swimming on Sunday too. Anyone interested?

lines.speaker: Sofia
lines.text: Me too. I've decided to start training for the school race.

items.why: start needs to or -ing, not the bare verb

can_do: I can use like, love, hate, enjoy and don't mind with the -ing form.
I can use want, need, would like, hope, decide and learn with to + base verb.
I can talk about activities with go + -ing and make suggestions with let's / how about + -ing.
summary: Like, love, hate, enjoy and don't mind are followed by the -ing form.
Want, need, would like, hope, decide and learn are followed by to + base verb.
Use go + -ing for sports and activities: go swimming, go shopping, go camping.
Start and begin can take either -ing or to, with the same meaning.
Make suggestions with let's, why don't we and how about + -ing.
